title: When does a scaling result justify a different allocation? A critical review of resource-allocation evidence for AI systems
abstract: arXiv:2609.14500v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI scaling studies increasingly evaluate systems that combine a pretrained model with retrieval, search, verification, tools, and interaction. Yet a higher score under a larger budget does not by itself show where additional resources are best spent. This critical integrative review asks when a reported scaling result supports a resource-allocation decision. It compares evidence across pretraining, test-time computation, retrieval, and agent evaluation, distinguishing the performance of a tested procedure from the best performance achievable under a resource limit. The synthesis shows that three mismatches recur across this evidence: success counted before an answer is chosen, information a deployed system will not have, and costs left out of the comparison. translated_title: 何时扩展结果才能证明不同资源配置的合理性？——对AI系统资源配置证据的批判性综述
translated_abstract: AI扩展研究越来越多地评估将预训练模型与检索、搜索、验证、工具和交互相结合的系统。然而，在更大预算下获得更高的分数本身并不能说明额外资源应该最佳地投向何处。这篇批判性整合综述探讨了这样一个问题：什么样的已报告扩展结果才能支持资源配置决策。该综述比较了预训练、测试时计算、检索和智能体评估等方面的证据，区分了被测程序的性能与在资源限制下可达到的最优性能。综合分析表明，这些证据中反复出现三种不匹配：在答案被选定之前就计算成功、使用了部署系统实际不会拥有的信息、以及在比较中遗漏了成本。文中提出“能力面”概念，将性能表示为预算、机制和可用信息的函数，并通过分析实例展示了评估指标、部署规模等因素的作用。
tldr: 该综述提出“能力面”分析框架，指出AI扩展证据中反复存在三种不匹配（提前计分、使用部署时不可得的信息、遗漏成本），并阐明只有克服这些缺陷的扩展结果才能为AI系统的资源配置决策提供正当依据。
en_tdlr: This critical review introduces a "capability surface" framework and identifies three recurring mismatches in AI scaling evidence—scoring success before an answer is chosen, using information unavailable to deployed systems, and omitting costs—to determine when scaling results can legitimately justify resource-allocation decisions.
